name: Bilt
summary: Bilt turns housing and neighborhood spending into a rewards and commerce network, with rent, mortgage, and local merchants as its core distribution channels.
overview: Bilt operates a rewards and commerce network built around housing spend. It works with property owners, residents, merchants, and financial partners to make rent, mortgage, and neighborhood spending a source of loyalty value.

facts.label: Reported valuation
facts.note: July 2025 primary financing; reported by the transaction adviser.

bull_case: Housing payments are frequent, high-value transactions that can create a durable loyalty relationship if Bilt can keep partners and members engaged.
bear_case: The model depends on complex partnerships, reward economics, and consumer credit behavior, all of which can pressure unit economics.
latest_round: July 2025: $250M primary financing at a reported $10.75B valuation
directory_notes: Housing spend, merchant adoption, and mortgage distribution.
Reward costs, partner concentration, and credit economics.

intelligence.description: Bilt is a housing-focused rewards and commerce platform that connects residents, property partners, financial institutions, and local merchants.
company: Bilt began by making rent payments rewardable, then expanded its proposition to housing-related and neighborhood commerce. The company works with property owners, residents, merchants, and financial partners, which makes the platform a combination of loyalty program, payments infrastructure, and consumer marketplace.

In July 2025, Bilt announced $250 million in new primary funding. FT Partners, which advised on the transaction, said the round valued Bilt at $10.75 billion and was led by General Catalyst and GID, with United Wholesale Mortgage participating in a strategic partnership.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Bilt is a useful private-market case study in whether an overlooked recurring expense can become a valuable distribution layer for financial services and commerce. Its performance is a read-through for loyalty economics, housing fintech, consumer credit, and merchant-funded rewards.

changed.text: Bilt launches a rewards proposition centered on rent payments.
Bilt announces $250M of primary funding at a reported $10.75B valuation.
A strategic partnership with United Wholesale Mortgage extends the company's housing focus toward mortgage distribution.

takeaways: Bilt's differentiator is access to a recurring housing-payment relationship rather than a conventional credit-card acquisition funnel.
The reported valuation assumes the network can expand from rent rewards into broader housing and local-commerce activity.
Financial partners and merchant economics are central to the model, so reward costs deserve close attention.
Its consumer brand is strong, but its long-term defensibility will depend on partner retention and repeat transaction behavior.
